phase: feed-disc co-tuning after the disc bore was opened
fixed_disc: 29 ridges, inner radius 8.0 mm (best of 6.2/8/10), +-84/84/34 mm domain, 3x12 deg spacers

comparison.finding: shrinking the feed radial envelope from 5.3875 to 4.925 mm adds 3 GHz of contiguous bandwidth and drops 28 GHz to -24.76 dB; only 32 GHz is still above -10 dB

open: 32 GHz at -8.18 dB needs another 2 dB; the running sweep tests radial 1.15/1.20/1.30
main beam is still at theta 40 deg, so the feed-disc focus/axial position is next
peak gain 4.18 dBi is still below the 5-8 dBi reference

radial_sweep.fixed: bore 8 mm, flare 1.5, inner step -0.25, 12 passes, MaxDeltaS 0.02
radial_sweep.finding: radial 1.25 and 1.30 both give 7.0 GHz contiguous; 1.30 matches 24-31 GHz deepest (28 GHz -26.63 dB, 24 GHz -12.38 dB) but 32 GHz is worst there (-7.05); radial 1.20 fixes 32 GHz (-9.41) yet breaks 24 and 30 GHz. The feed outer exit controls 32 GHz while the inner stages control 24/30, which is why an independent outer-exit scale was added to the builder.

radial_1p30.note: deepest 24-31 GHz match so far; 32 GHz is the only failure

run_isolation_defect.what: two measurement campaigns shared one AEDT session; both copy the template to lens28_var.aedt, so the second campaign's solve/export silently acted on the first campaign's still-open project
run_isolation_defect.symptom: radial 1.20 and 1.25 produced byte-identical S11 and far-field metrics
run_isolation_defect.fix: one variant per process: kill AEDT + guard daemons, start a single AEDT, build, measure, exit (run_variant_once.py)
run_isolation_defect.why_it_matters: without this, any parameter sweep run in one session is untrustworthy

plan: vary the disc ring pitch (disc_pitch_scale 0.90 / 1.10) at candidate 30 + radial 1.30: a denser or sparser corrugation should move the high-frequency edge that no feed parameter moved
then axial feed offset for the beam direction and the final acceptance table

outer_exit_scale.parameter: outer_radial_scale (pivot at the first stage radius; default 1.0 keeps the old geometry)
outer_exit_scale.purpose: decouple the 32 GHz behaviour from the 24/30 GHz matching

E1_result.note: shrinking the outer exit did not move 32 GHz (-7.87 vs -7.05) and the 24/25 Hz rows went missing from the export, so this lever is not the answer

disc_candidate_comparison.finding: candidate 26 gives the best gain so far (4.32 dBi) but only 3.0 GHz; candidate 30 with radial 1.30 remains the best bandwidth trade-off (7.0 GHz). The 32 GHz failure survives both discs and every feed-side parameter, pointing at the periodic ring layout itself.

builder_extensions.outer_radial_scale: outer feed exit scale at the first stage pivot (E1: did not fix 32 GHz)
builder_extensions.disc_pitch_scale: scales pitch/ridge width/first-ring origin of the corrugated disc; default 1.0

disc_pitch_scale.what: scales pitch, ridge width and first-ring origin of the corrugated disc (default 1.0)
disc_pitch_scale.finding: denser rings move the mismatch from 32 GHz to 30-31 GHz and make 32 GHz excellent (-14.06): the gap follows the corrugation pitch, so a sparser pitch (1.10) should push the gap above the band and is measuring now

P11_pitch1p10.note: sparser rings push the gap up: 32 GHz now passes (-10.29) and only 31 GHz fails (-8.42)

disc_pitch_scale.status: uniform pitch moves the gap but the gap stays inside 24-32 GHz (1.0 -> 32, 1.10 -> 31, 1.15 -> 30), so the builder now also supports disc_pitch_gradient: the ring pitch changes with radius so the stopband spreads instead of blocking one edge. G1 = gradient +0.25 is measuring.

P115_pitch1p15.note: gap moved to 30 GHz, 31 and 32 both pass, and peak gain reaches 5.09 dBi for the first time

disc_pitch_gradient.what: ring pitch varies linearly with radius (heights and taper unchanged); default 0 is the old geometry

G1_gradient0p25.note: too strong: the stopband splits into 29 and 32 GHz and the contiguous band shrinks to 4 GHz

disc_pitch_gradient.status: tested +0.25 and +0.10: both split/shrink the passband instead of smoothing it. A gradient in this form is not the fix; local changes confined to the outer few rings (or a wider band design of the disc) would be the next structural attempt.

G2_gradient0p10.note: a mild chirp also fails: 29 and 32 GHz dip, contiguous band 4.0 GHz. Uniform pitch 1.0 remains the widest contiguous band (7.0 GHz, 24-31).
